Now that the Skip column is created, I want to start implementing its function.
When reading a chapter and you have reached the end of the final page, if you click on the last page of that chapter normally you are taken to the first page of the next chapter.
After clicking on the last page, I want the program to check and see if the next chapter is marked as skipped. If it is then skip to the next chapter that is not marked as skipped and start reading that chapter. The Skip feature should not have any effect on any other part of the program besides the reading of chapters.
Use methods to repair and optimize the code.
Make sure any changes do not cause program errors. And do not cause errors in Lint and Release.

```
The pagination state is now controlled and only resets on series changes, not on checkbox updates. I’m validating the chapter table file first, then desktop and workspace lint/build.The file diagnostics and desktop lint are clean. I’m reading the build result and then I’ll run root lint/build to match your release-safety requirement.The table fix is in and desktop checks are clean so far. I’m running workspace-level lint and build now to make sure the pagination state change doesn’t regress the broader release path.Root lint passed. I’m reading the captured root build result now to confirm the final exit code, then I’ll clean up the temporary logs.The workspace build log shows the desktop package completed and Turbo finished successfully. I’m removing the temporary verification logs so the branch stays clean, then I’ll summarize the fix.Fixed the chapter list pagination reset. The list will now stay on the current page when you toggle checkboxes, including the Skip column.

What changed:
1. I converted the chapter table pagination to controlled state in `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/library/series/chapter-table/ChapterTable.tsx`.
2. I disabled TanStack Table’s automatic page-index reset with  in `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/library/series/chapter-table/ChapterTable.tsx`.
3. I added a clamp so if the current page ever becomes invalid because the list shrinks, it moves to the last valid page instead of jumping to page one.
4. I kept the page reset only for series changes by resetting  to `0` when  changes. That matches your requirement that page one should only happen when opening a Series page fresh from elsewhere, or when you manually pick page one yourself.

Why this fixes your issue:
Before this change, updating chapter data after clicking a checkbox caused the table to rebuild and its internal pagination state to reset. Now pagination lives in React state, so checkbox updates do not send the table back to page one.

Validation:

2. Desktop lint: passed
3. Desktop build: passed
4. Root lint: passed
5. Root build: passed

This change is scoped to chapter table pagination only. It does not change Skip behavior, reader behavior, or any other list behavior outside preserving the current page during data updates.
